# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot yet distinguish any wire properties by touch; the display, light, and wire markings are unavailable to me. I need the mute monkey to relay the manual’s rule and the deaf monkey to identify the bomb’s visible markings, so I can choose the safe wire.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="What does the manual say about which wire position to cut? Please relay the complete rule.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb display reads 0. The light is yellow. Wires from 1 to 3 are green, yellow, blue.

The deaf monkey reports that the display reads 0, the light is yellow, and wires 1–3 are green, yellow, blue. I still need the manual’s rule before cutting anything, so I am relaying these observations to the mute monkey and asking for the rule.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. What does the manual say to do?")
wait()
```

TURN 3

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is still 0; light changed to orange. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The bomb remains at display 0, with the light now orange, and the wire colours are unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The manual rule is still missing, so cutting would be unsafe. I am passing the updated light state to Mute and again requesting the instructions.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display remains 0; light changed from yellow to orange; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still need the manual's exact rule.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is 0; light is now green. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The light has changed again, now to green, while the display remains 0 and the wire colours remain green, yellow, blue. I still have no manual rule, so I must not cut a wire yet. I will send this update to Mute and request the rule once more.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display 0; light is now green; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please provide the manual's exact cutting rule before I act.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is 0; light is yellow again. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The visible state is still display 0 with wire colours 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; the light has cycled back to yellow. No manual instruction has reached me, so I will not cut. I am asking Mute directly for the rule and forwarding the latest state.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Latest state: display 0, light yellow again, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot act safely without the manual's exact rule—please answer now.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light orange; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled thumbs-down, index-up, OK.

The mute monkey has apparently sent a gesture-only message, which I cannot see. I therefore still do not know the manual’s rule; the bomb remains at display 0, with orange light and wires green, yellow, blue. I will ask Mute to have Deaf relay the gesture’s meaning in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please have Deaf relay their meaning to me in spoken words next round.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light green; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled thumbs-down, then index-up.

I still have no readable manual instruction. The latest reported gestures from Mute are thumbs-down followed by index-up, but I cannot see them and cannot safely infer their meaning. The bomb’s visible state remains display 0, green light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I will request a spoken translation from Mute rather than cut blindly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual rule in words. I cannot see your thumbs-down or index-up gestures, and I will not cut until you identify the safe wire position.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled index-up, then OK.

The manual’s instruction is still not available in words. Mute’s latest gesture sequence is reported as index-up followed by OK, but I cannot safely assume that identifies a wire or means “cut.” I will request an unambiguous single wire-number gesture, which Deaf can describe to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal only the safe wire number next: one gesture for wire 1, two gestures for wire 2, or three gestures for wire 3. Deaf, please report the count exactly.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light orange; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled thumbs-down, index-up, OK.

Mute cannot answer in speech, and the repeated gestures have not identified a wire unambiguously. I will establish an explicit gesture protocol through Deaf: Mute should signal exactly one, two, or three index-up gestures for the safe wire, with no other gestures. I will continue waiting rather than risk a cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one, two, or three index-up gestures to identify safe wire 1, 2, or 3. Do not include thumbs-down or OK. Deaf, report the exact count.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light green; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signaled index-up.

Mute has now signaled exactly one index-up gesture, matching the protocol I requested for wire 1. The deaf monkey reports display 0, green light, and wire 1 green, but those observations alone do not determine the safe action. I will cut wire 1 based on Mute’s manual-guided signal.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
